rows.citation: Makarov R., Chavlis S., Poirazi P. (2025). DendroTweaks, an interactive approach for unraveling dendritic dynamics. eLife 13:RP103324.
rows.model_type: multicompartmental conductance-based single-cell models with active dendrites (NEURON MOD + SWC; Jaxley backend demonstrated)
rows.controlled_mutations: no; manual parameter edits (e.g., HCN block as 80% conductance reduction, removing sodium channels) illustrate mechanisms, not systematic single-fault injection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes; built-in semi-automated protocols: hyperpolarizing steps, depolarizing steps, f-I current series, synaptic input series, somatic and dendritic injection.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes; time constant, input resistance, sag ratio, AP amplitude/half-width, firing rate, f-I curve, dendritic nonlinearity; own implementation, eFEL not used.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; users choose protocols and stimulus parameters; no search for compact or discriminating protocol sets.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; demonstrations on three replicated published models (Park 2019, Poirazi 2003, Hay 2011); no discovery/held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-generated or agent-performed model edits are evaluated.
rows.software: DendroTweaks https://github.com/Poirazi-Lab/DendroTweaks (PyPI dendrotweaks 0.5.2; library code MPL-2.0 from v0.5.0)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Offers visual before/after trace comparison for channel standardization, morphology reduction and NEURON-vs-Jaxley runs, but no calibrated automatic divergence detection, mutants, protocol selection or held-out evaluation; not NeuroML/LEMS based.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, authors, eLife vol 13, RP103324, 2025-12-23); Europe PMC full text PMC12726829 (validation protocols, standardization, Jaxley sections); OpenAlex record; GitHub REST API, README and repo tree; PyPI JSON API.
rows.found_via: GitHub search neuron model validation (Poirazi-Lab/DendroTweaks, MPL-2.0); DOI in README verified via Crossref works API; PyPI dendrotweaks 0.5.2

rows.citation: rhkrohan [GitHub user; individual authors unverified] (2025). NeuroForgeAI: end-to-end computational neuroscience toolkit for building optimized biophysical neuron models from experimental recordings. GitHub.
rows.model_type: morphologically detailed NEURON e-model (SWC morphology + HH-type MOD channels) fitted to recordings with BluePyOpt/BluePyEFE
rows.controlled_mutations: partial; sensitivity script varies each parameter +/-20% and records feature changes; exploratory sensitivity, not recorded single-fault mutants with detection classification.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes; scripts implement step families, ramp, three-pulse burst and sine stimulation; README also describes noise injection.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes; README lists eFEL/BluePyEFE features (spike count, AP amplitude, ISI, adaptation, sag); some test scripts use simple threshold spike counts.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; CMA-ES optimizes model parameters, not the choice of test protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear; README claims validation on held-out data and independent protocols, but inspected model_evaluation.py shows no train/test split logic.
rows.ai_transformations: no; despite the name, inspected README and scripts evaluate no AI-performed model edits or translations.
rows.software: NeuroForgeAI https://github.com/rhkrohan/NeuroForgeAI (README states MIT, but no LICENSE file; GitHub API license null)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: A small fitting pipeline whose multi-stimulus and sensitivity checks assess fit quality of one model. NeuroSem tests behaviour preservation after edits/translations with refinement-calibrated tolerances, mutant classification, protocol selection and held-out splits.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repo metadata, tree and contributors; raw README.md, model_evaluation/README.md, model_evaluation.py, scripts/sensitivity_analysis.py, advanced_stimulation_tests.py, ci.yml; LICENSE URL returned 404.

rows.citation: OpenSourceBrain [GitHub organization; individual authors unverified] (2016). PyNNShowcase: a repository for testing interactions/conversions between NeuroML & PyNN. GitHub.
rows.model_type: Izhikevich and simple point-neuron/small network examples in NeuroML2/LEMS and PyNN
rows.controlled_mutations: no; no fault injection; OMV tests only check that each engine reproduces expected spike times.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; a few example scenarios (current input, spike sources, connections), each test fixed to one scenario.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; only threshold-detected spike times compared with expected lists in OMV .mep files under a numeric tolerance.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; continuous-integration regression tests, no evaluation split.
rows.software: PyNNShowcase https://github.com/OpenSourceBrain/PyNNShowcase (no license file detected); tests run with OMV https://github.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Cross-engine conversion regression (jNeuroML, NEURON, NEST, Brian2 via PyNN) on stored spike times; a form of translation-equivalence checking. NeuroSem adds multi-protocol feature fingerprints, refinement-calibrated tolerances, mutant sensitivity, protocol selection and holdouts.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API (repo metadata, recursive tree, contributors via gh api); raw README.md, NeuroML2 and PyNN .omt/.mep files, .github/workflows/omv-ci.yml.

rows.citation: OpenSourceBrain [GitHub organization; individual authors unverified] (2014). AllenInstituteNeuroML: example files to test interaction between models developed at the Allen Brain Institute and NeuroML. GitHub.
rows.model_type: Allen Cell Types Database models: biophysical NEURON cells and GLIF point neurons, converted to NeuroML2/LEMS
rows.controlled_mutations: no; no seeded faults; tests compare converted or re-run models against expected spike times.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; current-clamp sweeps from Allen data and voltage-ramp channel analyses exist, but each OMV test uses one sweep.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; threshold spike times in OMV tests; a script plots NeuroML vs MOD channel time constants for manual comparison.
rows.software: AllenInstituteNeuroML https://github.com/OpenSourceBrain/AllenInstituteNeuroML (LICENSE file: MIT for OSB code, Allen-derived content excluded; GitHub reports NOASSERTION); OMV engines NEURON, jNeuroML, jNeuroML_NEURON, jNeuroML_NetPyNE
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Conversion regression across simulators on spike times plus manual channel-kinetics plots; also a possible fixture source (Allen content licensing needs checking). NeuroSem adds systematic feature fingerprints, calibrated tolerances, mutants, protocol selection and holdouts.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API (metadata, license endpoint, recursive tree via gh api); raw README.md, LICENSE, CITATION.md, compare_nml2_mods.py, .omt/.mep files, omv-ci.yml and non-omv.yml workflows. Zenodo DOI badge unverified (HTTP 504).

rows.citation: NeuroML [GitHub organization; individual authors unverified] (2017). mod2neuroml: pipelines for generating NeuroML2/LEMS from mod files (NEURON simulator). GitHub.
rows.model_type: NMODL ion-channel mechanisms to NeuroML2/LEMS (conversion route notes)
rows.controlled_mutations: no; repository contains only a README.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no; no test or simulation content in the repository.
rows.software: mod2neuroml https://github.com/NeuroML/mod2neuroml (README only; no license file); points to pynmodl https://github.com/borismarin/pynmodl and pyNeuroML channel-analysis tools
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: A pointer document to NMODL-to-NeuroML conversion routes with no behavioural checking. Relevant only as a source of translation transformations whose behaviour preservation NeuroSem could test.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API (metadata, recursive tree showing a single README.md, contributors via gh api); raw README.md.

rows.citation: Akolekar N., Singh A. (2018). mod2nml: NMODL to NeuroML language translator. GitHub.
rows.model_type: NMODL ion-channel files to NeuroML (lexer plus template translator; course project)
rows.multiple_stimuli: no; inspected source runs no simulations.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; no evaluation of translated versus original behaviour found.
rows.software: mod2nml https://github.com/ninadakolekar/mod2nml (archived; no license file detected)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: An unvalidated NMODL-to-NeuroML translator; NeuroSem does not translate but would test whether such translations preserve electrophysiological behaviour under multiple protocols.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API (metadata incl. archived flag, recursive tree, contributors via gh api); raw README.md (names collaborators Ninad Akolekar and Ankur Singh), src/translator.py, src/app.py.
